Peripheral blood sample from an 86-year-old man with borderline lymphocytosis (2.8 × 109/L), haemoglobin 134 g/L, platelet count 252, no palpable lymphadenopathy, and B cells 1.0 × 109/L: the chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL)-type MBL cells are red, CD5+ non-CLL MBL cells are brown, and residual normal polyclonal mature B cells are green; the CLL/SLL-type MBL cells are CD19+, CD20weak/+, light chain−/weak, CD5+, CD23+, CD200+, CD43+, CD79b−/weak, ROR1+, CD81−/weak, CD22+/weak, and CD25+, and the CD5+ non–CLL/SLL-type MBL cells are CD19+, CD20+, kappa light chain+, CD5+, CD23−, CD200−, CD43+/weak, CD79b+, ROR1+, CD81+/weak, CD22+/weak, and CD25+. These cells display the phenotype of mantle cell lymphoma, and FISH analysis of CD19-selected cells demonstrated a CCND1::IGH translocation. Therefore, this case represents a composite proliferation of (leukaemic, non-nodal) mantle cell lymphoma and low-count MBL (CLL/SLL phenotype) with a clone size of < 0.5 × 109/L.
